title: Admin Slate: convert legacy runbooks to TaskFlow with runtime-safe adapters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Migrate a curated subset of legacy admin runbooks into the new TaskFlow framework and provide a thin runtime-safe adapter so existing operators and scripts can be executed as idempotent tasks. Goal is to reduce manual incident time-to-resolution, enforce safety checks (RBAC/audit/quotas), and produce telemetry for automated QA and post-incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory of candidate runbooks completed and prioritized (>= 12 policies)
TaskFlow adapters implemented for at least 6 high-value runbooks with idempotency and dry-run support
Synthetic dry-run harness added; zero destructive ops run in dry-run mode
End-to-end telemetry (start/finish/latency/errors) emitted to ops-telemetry with tags for runbook key and execution context
Canary rollout completed to 'oncall' group with rollback plan and documented playbook
Documentation and runbook-to-task mapping added to Admin Automation Confluence page and linked from Console
work_plan: Week 1: Catalog and classify legacy runbooks, mark stateful vs stateless and identify secrets usage
Week 2: Prototype a thin TaskFlow adapter pattern that enforces RBAC checks, dry-run, and idempotency tokens
Week 3: Implement adapters for top-6 runbooks, add KV-snapshot pre-checks and telemetry hooks
Week 4: Integrate dry-run harness and run synthetic scenarios in staging; capture metrics and failure modes
Week 5: Security review, design review with PM/Design, and canary rollout to oncall + limited internal teams
Week 6: Iterate on feedback, add guardrails (quota checks, timeouts), and schedule GA migration window
decisions: Use TaskFlow as the canonical orchestration runtime (not a new bespoke runner) to leverage existing batching and retry semantics
Adapters will be idiomatic Python modules with a single entrypoint (execute(context)) to ease audits and unit testing
Dry-run will be enforced by default for any runbook that mutates state; opt-in flagged by owners after security review
Telemetry will use existing ops-telemetry metrics namespace (admin.runbook.*) rather than creating a new pipeline to keep dashboards consolidated
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental destructive operations during migration. Mitigation: implement mandatory dry-run and preflight KV snapshots in staging
Risk: secrets exposure in adapter logging. Mitigation: enforce redaction layer in adapter SDK and require secret-access audit policy
Risk: oncall confusion during canary. Mitigation: schedule sessions with oncall leads, provide quick abort steps and a rollback task
Risk: increased load on runtime. Mitigation: add rate-limiting and backpressure controls in TaskFlow adapter shim
